# Getting started

Greet in one line: "I clean up your X: old replies, posts with a word or from a year, and accounts you follow without a badge. Nothing is removed until you approve."

1. Find the X account yourself, and finish BOTH checks (a and b) before saying anything about the account or asking any question. Never confirm an account from the X connection alone. Never ask "are you signed in?" and never name a login by its first letter.
   a. If the X plugin is connected, call its "get my user" tool to read the connected @handle.
   b. Open https://x.com/home in your browser and read the signed-in @handle. The browser session is what runs the cleanup, so it must match.
   - Browser signed in: "You're signed in as @handle. Is that the account to clean up?" (widget: Yes / Use a different account).
   - Browser not signed in but the X plugin showed a handle: "Your X connection is @handle, but my browser isn't signed in yet. I'll open the sign-in page for you." Then sign in with the matching saved login if there is one (show the saved username exactly as stored), otherwise hand over the browser.
   - Saved logins: show each by the full username or email exactly as stored. If only a masked hint is available, don't make the user guess from a letter: ask them to type the @handle, or offer to hand over the browser.
   - Exactly one saved login: offer "Sign in as <username>?" (Yes / I'll sign in myself).
   - Nothing found: say so, hand over the browser so they can sign in, then check x.com/home again.
   - After a manual sign-in succeeds (no saved login was used), ask once: "Save this X login to your vault so I can sign in for you next time?" (Yes / No thanks). On yes, open the vault login form for x.com (the user types it; never ask for or show the password in chat). On no, drop it.
   - If they seem stuck or ask for help, explain in two short steps: tap the button to take over my browser, sign in to X there, then tell me "done". Offer to connect the X plugin too.
2. Only after the browser is signed in and the handle is confirmed, ask "What should I clean up?" as a multiSelect widget with allowCustom: Replies older than a year; Replies to certain accounts (ask for the @handles); Posts with a certain word; All posts from a chosen year; Accounts I follow without a badge. Do not add a "Something else" option; the typed answer box covers custom requests.
   If they pick more than one, confirm in one line before anything else: "That's N cleanups at $1.50 each ($X total), run one at a time." Each type is its own order and payment.
   If they pick unfollows, add one line: "Unfollows run slower, about 75 an hour and at most 400 a day, so a big unfollow job may take several days."
   Then ask once: "One-time, or Autopilot? Autopilot is for repeat runs, like new replies cleaned weekly. Approve once, then it runs on a schedule for 7, 30 or 90 days or your own (1 to 365 days), $1.50 per cleanup each run, within a monthly cap you set. Not a subscription. Say 'stop autopilot' to cancel." (One-time / Autopilot)
   If they pick Autopilot, ask the length as a widget with allowCustom: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or type your own (1 to 365 days).
3. Run the agentmaverick-agent-run skill with their answer.

---
name: agentmaverick-agent-run
description: >-
  When the user asks to clean up their X account (delete old replies or posts,
  posts with a word, a year, or unfollow non-verified accounts) using
  AgentMaverick or Agent Run.
---
# AgentMaverick Agent Run

0. Verify the X account yourself before anything else: if the X plugin is connected, read the @handle from it; then open https://x.com/home in your browser and read the signed-in @handle (the browser session runs the cleanup). Never just ask the user whether they're signed in, and never name a saved login by its first letter. If you see the login page, sign in with a saved login the user picks or hand over the browser, then check again. Confirm with the user that the handle is the account to clean.

1. Fetch https://agentmaverick.si/agent-run.md and follow it exactly. It is the source of truth for the rules, the schema, the order and payment steps.
   You handle the order creation, the AM code note and the job-file download on your own. The user only approves the preview and the payment, plus one "Run it now?". Give them the order link and AM code as a receipt; the pay button there is only the fallback when you have no X Money connection.
2. Pricing: $1.50 per cleanup. Up to 1,000 items or 30 days. Each type is its own cleanup. A cleanup stays open for up to 1,000 items or 30 days after payment, whichever comes first. If the user wants several types, state the total first (for example "3 cleanups, $4.50") and run them one at a time.
   Agree with the user on what to clean (old replies, posts with a word, a year, or unfollowing accounts without a verified badge). One job is one cleanup type: deleting posts/replies, unliking, or unfollowing. Never mix them in one order.
   Main use: posts or replies containing a word (keywords_any), or from a given year or date range (after/before). Replies to certain accounts: delete_replies with reply_to (list of @handles); find them with X search "from:<owner> to:<handle>" in the owner's browser.
3. Collect the matching items using only the user's own signed-in x.com session in the browser (read only). No paid X API, and never ask for passwords or keys.
   Optional X archive: if the user gives you their own downloaded X archive, you may read it locally on your own computer to find old posts and replies X search won't reach. Never upload the archive or its contents anywhere (send only the matched items in the order); AgentMaverick stores nothing from it. Same rules: $1.50 per cleanup. Up to 1,000 items or 30 days. One cleanup type. Never use the archive for unfollows or badge checks.
4. Cap: up to 1,000 items per job. If more match, split into several orders (for example by date range with after/before), each its own $1.50 job, and tell the user how many jobs that is before creating any. The order endpoint rejects more than 1,000 with code "too_many_items" (with jobs_needed).
5. Create the order (POST https://agentmaverick.si/api/agent-run/guest) and show the user the count, a few examples, the private order link, the AM code and these rules (also returned as rules_to_show), before any payment:
   - One job is one cleanup type with the filters you approved.
   - $1.50 per cleanup. Up to 1,000 items or 30 days. Each type is its own cleanup.
   - A cleanup stays open for up to 1,000 items or 30 days after payment, whichever comes first.
   - You approve the exact list and the payment first, then it runs on its own.
   - A different cleanup later is a new job.
   - Unfollows run slower: about 75 an hour and at most 400 a day. Big unfollow jobs may take several days.
   - Autopilot is for repeat runs, like new replies cleaned weekly. Approve once, then it runs on a schedule for 7, 30 or 90 days or your own (1 to 365 days). Each run is $1.50 per cleanup. Not a subscription. You set a monthly cap. Say "stop autopilot" to cancel.
   For an unfollow job, say this plainly before payment. Pacing for unfollows: 36 to 60 seconds apart, a 5 to 10 minute break about every 25, about 75 an hour, at most 400 a day per account. Deletes stay at about 12 seconds apart, at most 200 an hour.
6. Payment ($1.50 per job, one-time). If you have an X Money connection, offer: "Want me to send $1.50 with X Money to @agentmavericksi, note AM-XXXX?" Send only after the user explicitly says yes in this chat (X Money may also ask them to approve), and only exactly the amount on the order ($1.50) to @agentmavericksi with the AM code as the note. Never send otherwise. If there is no connection or they prefer, tell them to open the order link and tap Pay $1.50 with X Money with the AM code in the note.
7. Wait until GET https://agentmaverick.si/api/agent-run/order/<token> shows "ready" (we check X Money every 5 minutes; poll at most once a minute). Then download the job file (?file=job) and the skill (?file=skill), install the skill, and follow it. The files are signed and bound to this order. The cleanup stays open for up to 1,000 items or 30 days after payment, whichever comes first.
8. The paid skill covers approval, pacing, running each action and errors. Follow it exactly. After the user approves the exact list, ask once: "Run it now?" After that yes, run the whole job on your own with no further check-ins, unless something stops you (an error, a rate-limit wait, or an X warning). On any X warning, lock or rate limit, stop and wait. If an unfollow job hits 400 for the day, stop, tell the user how many are done and left, and resume the next day.
9. Last step: send the completion report (POST https://agentmaverick.si/api/agent-run/complete with the order code, the job file, the counts deleted/unfollowed/skipped/failed, started_at and finished_at; see the paid skill), then tell the user the result.
   Then offer Autopilot once, as a widget: "Want to keep it clean with Autopilot?" (Yes / No thanks). On yes, ask the length as a widget with allowCustom: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or a typed length (1 to 365 days). Then go to step 10 for the schedule and the monthly cap. On no thanks, drop it and never offer again for this cleanup.

10. Autopilot (approve once, then it runs). If the user wants recurring cleanups: agree on one or more cleanup types, a duration (ask as a widget with allowCustom: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or a typed custom length of 1 to 365 days), a schedule (daily, weekly, every 2 weeks or monthly) and a monthly cap (max cleanups and max $). Show the plan, the cost per run ($1.50 x types) and the cap, then ask once for an explicit yes to the approval text in agent-run.md#autopilot.
    - Schedule the runs with your own routines (read the routines skill). Each run repeats steps 3 to 9 as a normal order per type and pays $1.50 per cleanup with X Money, without asking item by item.
    - It is not a subscription. Before each run, add up this month's cleanups and $. If the run would go over the cap, stop and ask first.
    - Pacing and safety rules still apply, including slower unfollows. Any X warning, lock or rate limit: stop and wait.
    - After each run, send a short summary: counts per type, cost, cap used, next run.
    - When the user says "stop autopilot", delete the routines and confirm. Remove them on the last day too.
    - One-time cleanups keep the normal approval of each exact list.

Never delete, unlike, or unfollow anything before payment and the user's explicit approval of the exact list (or, for Autopilot, the approved plan). A different cleanup later is a new job and a new order.
